note: Hand-written by the thread's model in the Assayer's persona. The five judged scores (1 to 5) are opinions, graded Suspected; effort 1 is one session, 5 is many sessions or needs hardware. Flags and graders are claims the assay tests; evidence paths are checked against local checkouts.

frontiers.title: Quality-diversity evolution of X3D scenes (MAP-Elites, novelty search)
frontiers.gain: An archive of valid-but-strange scenes that no person would write: every cell that one reader accepts and another breaks is a new receipt, found without a model call.
frontiers.first_step: Evolve 200 generations over a 12-node vocabulary; fitness is admitted by the gate and renders non-black; keep one judge held out so the search cannot learn it.

grader.name: x3d_mcp validator + loom traps + render non-black check

frontiers.title: Shape grammars and L-systems as scene programs
frontiers.gain: A scene becomes a short program with a known answer, so every generated file carries its own exact reference.
frontiers.first_step: Write a 5-rule L-system turtle to X3D; witness = predicted segment count equals counted Shape nodes at depths 1 to 7.

grader.name: exact symbol counts and Euler characteristic of the derivation

frontiers.title: Canonical form for X3D (equality saturation: one scene, one spelling)
frontiers.gain: Byte identity stops lying: two files that mean the same scene hash the same, which every dedupe, cache and receipt needs.
frontiers.first_step: Define 12 rewrite rules (default-field removal, DEF renaming, transform folding); prove the canoniser is idempotent on the 514-file sweep corpus.

grader.name: round-trip fixed point + semantic hash equality

frontiers.title: Solver-checked laws: prove the 44 laws and the r2r rules do not contradict
frontiers.gain: A contradiction between two rules is found by proof before a project trips on it; each rule gets a machine-readable form.
frontiers.first_step: Encode the 28 r2r candidate rules as SMT constraints and ask for any file that two rules grade differently.

grader.name: solver SAT and UNSAT certificates (Z3, pySHACL)

frontiers.title: Coverage-guided fuzzing of every X3D reader (Atheris, cargo-fuzz)
frontiers.gain: Chaos rounds found 68 crashes with blind one-edit mutants; coverage guidance reaches the branches blind mutation never touches.
frontiers.first_step: Wrap the x3d_mcp parser and the add-on's field coercion in Atheris harnesses; seed from tests/golden; 1 CPU-hour.

grader.name: crash oracle + six differential judges

frontiers.title: Cross-engine differential rendering as the oracle
frontiers.gain: Six renderers vote on every scene; a lone dissenter is a bug report with a picture, and agreement is evidence no single engine can give.
frontiers.first_step: Render the 30 conformance scenes in 3 engines with a fixed rig; publish the disagreement matrix and the 5 largest pixel gaps.

grader.name: X_ITE, three.js, Babylon, Castle, x3d.wgpu and Blender pixel difference

frontiers.title: Geometry-processing witnesses (manifold, Euler characteristic, self-intersection)
frontiers.gain: Mesh truth that a validator never checks: a schema-valid IndexedFaceSet can still be inside out, open or self-crossing.
frontiers.first_step: Add `kit/loom mesh`: 6 identities with 12 planted defects; sweep every IndexedFaceSet in x3d.demo.

grader.name: exact topological identities (V - E + F, closed manifold, winding)

frontiers.title: Implicit fields and cellular automata to mesh (SDF, marching cubes, reaction-diffusion)
frontiers.gain: Organic form with an exact discrete reference: the automaton's own state is the answer the mesh must match.
frontiers.first_step: 3D Gray-Scott to marching cubes to X3D; witness = voxel count above threshold equals enclosed-cell count.

grader.name: conserved quantity and step hash of the automaton

frontiers.title: Stigmergic builders: simple agents weaving a scene by local rules
frontiers.gain: Shows emergence under receipts, and gives the Gobbler's shell its tenders; little new law.
frontiers.first_step: 500 agents lay threads on a sphere by pheromone rule; Node and Chromium must agree on every step hash.

grader.name: deterministic step hash replayed in two hosts

frontiers.title: Active experiment design: the r2r needs list picks the next run (bandits, expected information gain)
frontiers.gain: The flywheel chooses its own next experiment by what would settle the most open rules per minute of instrument time.
frontiers.first_step: Rank the current `r2r needs` list by expected rules settled; run the top 5 and the bottom 5; compare rules settled.

grader.name: candidate rules closed or promoted per instrument-hour

frontiers.title: Topological data analysis of scene corpora (persistent homology)
frontiers.gain: A shape fingerprint for whole corpora; interesting, but few receipts flow back.
frontiers.first_step: Persistence diagrams for 50 demo meshes; plant 5 topology changes and check each moves the diagram.

grader.name: persistence diagram equality against a reference library (GUDHI)

frontiers.title: Text to X3D with the validator in the loop (repair from refusal codes)
frontiers.gain: Each refusal code a model cannot repair is a missing hint; each repaired one is a tested technique. Already the Gobbler's inner loop.
frontiers.first_step: Run the 35-signal sim day with a real model, memory on and off; report first-attempt admission with 3 trials per signal.

grader.name: x3d_mcp validator + loom traps on every attempt

frontiers.title: Grammar-constrained decoding: compile the X3D schema into a grammar so a small model cannot emit an invalid scene
frontiers.gain: Moves validity from repair to construction, and measures exactly which rules a grammar can carry (containment) and which it cannot (ROUTE types, DEF before USE).
frontiers.first_step: Compile the Interchange profile to GBNF; run a small open model 200 times with and without it; count validator passes.

grader.name: validity rate with and without the grammar, same model and seed

frontiers.title: Image and text to 3D models (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D, TripoSR class) into X3D with receipts
frontiers.gain: Generative meshes are the dirtiest input the Loom will ever see: non-manifold, baked light, no scale. Each defect class becomes a trap.
frontiers.first_step: Take 20 open-licence generated GLBs through Loom-for-glTF to X3D; census the defects by class.

grader.name: geometry witnesses + loss receipt on the converted mesh

frontiers.title: Gaussian splats and radiance fields into X3D 4.1
frontiers.gain: Photoreal capture inside the accountable format; the open question is what a receipt for a splat even counts.
frontiers.first_step: Define 5 splat witnesses (count, bounds, SH degree, opacity histogram, transform carried) with planted defects.

grader.name: splat render agreement across two viewers

frontiers.title: Generative shader art behind a compile-and-render guard (GLSL, WGSL)
frontiers.gain: Shaders are where validators go blind; a guard that compiles, links and renders closes the gap the shader fixture guard admits it leaves.
frontiers.first_step: Extend the 5-fixture shader guard to compile and render; evolve 100 fragment shaders under it.

grader.name: glslang and naga compile + lavapipe render hash

frontiers.title: Generated PBR materials and textures
frontiers.gain: Pretty, but narrow: one witness (energy conservation) and a licence question per texture.
frontiers.first_step: Generate 20 materials; run the white furnace; count the ones that create light.

grader.name: white-furnace energy test on every generated material

frontiers.title: Interactive evolution: you breed scenes by eye and your picks become the judge's labels
frontiers.gain: Turns your taste into data. Thirty picks is the label set the Assayer says a picture judge needs before it may grade anything (thesis T5).
frontiers.first_step: A 3 by 3 breeding page over the mascot's own genome; every click writes one signed preference row.

grader.name: your picks, recorded as labels with position swapped

frontiers.title: Video and world models to X3D (the 8-second stage)
frontiers.gain: Largest wow, weakest grip: no code grader exists yet and licences are restrictive.
frontiers.first_step: Hold until a judge passes kappa; then one 8-second clip to a staged scene.

grader.name: picture judge, not yet validated

frontiers.title: Audio-reactive generative scenes
frontiers.gain: A solved pattern here; re-use more than new learning.
frontiers.first_step: Bind the mascot's fan to the existing Loomsong onsets.

grader.name: onset alignment between score and keyframes

frontiers.title: Procedural worlds: wave function collapse, noise terrain, erosion, cities
frontiers.gain: A generator whose every output is checkable by its own constraints; feeds Accrete with admitted worlds.
frontiers.first_step: WFC with 12 tiles on a 20 cubed grid; witness = 0 illegal adjacencies; admit through the Accrete gate.

grader.name: constraint satisfaction count (every tile adjacency legal)

frontiers.title: A public scoreboard of models on Loom tasks
frontiers.gain: The Loom's failure modes become an exam any model can sit. It is the one artefact outsiders can cite, and each model's misses are fresh receipts.
frontiers.first_step: Freeze 60 tasks from failure modes that have a code grader; hold 12 private; score 3 trials per task.

grader.name: validator + traps + hidden reference answers

frontiers.title: DSPy and GEPA optimisation of the rule proposer
frontiers.gain: An optimiser writes better prompts than we do, but it optimises whatever the grader rewards, so the grader must stay hidden.
frontiers.first_step: Switch on the r2r proposer seam for the `needs` list only; cap at Suspected; under $10.

grader.name: r2r self-test (hidden rules recovered word for word)

frontiers.title: Retrieval over the Loom: the right law and failure mode on the page before the first line is written
frontiers.gain: 213 failure modes are useless unread. Retrieval at kickoff makes every past receipt pay again; lexical first, so no model call.
frontiers.first_step: Build BM25 over laws, failure modes and LEARNINGS; write 40 questions from real incidents; measure recall at 5.

grader.name: recall at 5 on held-out failure-mode questions

frontiers.title: Fine-tune a small open model on validator-labelled Loom data
frontiers.gain: Every receipt is a labelled training row. A small model that writes valid X3D on your own GPU is the flywheel with no rented model in it.
frontiers.first_step: Export 5,000 (prompt, scene, verdict) rows with the dataset tools; LoRA on the G4; compare to the base model on 60 held tasks.

grader.name: validator pass rate on a held-out task split

frontiers.title: A picture judge calibrated against your eye
frontiers.gain: Beauty is your top criterion and the one thing no code grader sees. A judge is allowed only after it agrees with you.
frontiers.first_step: Collect 30 pair labels (see breed-judge); measure Cohen's kappa and a position-swap test before any use.

grader.name: vision model, valid only after kappa against your labels

frontiers.title: Builder, breaker and referee: a small swarm arguing over one scene
frontiers.gain: Tests the one thesis the Gobbler never has (T9: swarms change the threat model). Costly, and easy to fool yourself.
frontiers.first_step: Simulate first with scripted agents; measure whether a peer's instruction can override the referee.

grader.name: validator on the final scene; group behaviour unmeasured

frontiers.title: Scene embeddings and graph networks: similarity, dedupe and a map of every scene
frontiers.gain: A map of the corpus you can fly through; useful once the corpus is big.
frontiers.first_step: Hand-built 64-number structural fingerprint (node histogram, depth, ROUTE motifs); plant 50 near-duplicates.

grader.name: retrieval of 50 planted near-duplicates

frontiers.title: X3D as a synthetic-data factory for vision models
frontiers.gain: The scene graph knows every label for free. This is how X3D earns a seat in machine-learning pipelines.
frontiers.first_step: Render 1,000 randomised scenes with per-pixel node ids; witness = label image matches a second renderer.

grader.name: labels exact by construction (segmentation, depth, pose from the scene graph)

frontiers.title: X3D worlds as reinforcement-learning environments
frontiers.gain: X3D as the level format for agents. Reward hacking is the known hazard, which is why it teaches.
frontiers.first_step: Wrap the Rapier marble scene as a Gymnasium environment; random policy; 1,000 episodes replay bit-identically.

grader.name: step-hash determinism + reward from simulator state

frontiers.title: The token economy of X3D: which encoding can a model afford
frontiers.gain: Tells every agent how much scene fits in a context, and which encoding (XML, JSON, ClassicVRML, DEF/USE folded) costs least for the same scene.
frontiers.first_step: Count tokens for 100 scenes in 5 encodings with an open tokenizer; check each decodes to the same canonical scene.

grader.name: open-tokenizer counts + round-trip equality

frontiers.title: The Loom as an MCP server: laws, failure modes and r2r check as tools any agent can call
frontiers.gain: Any agent, in any product, gets the Loom's memory at the moment it needs it. The widest reuse per line of code.
frontiers.first_step: Expose 4 read-only tools (law, failure mode, trap check, r2r check) beside the validator; 20 contract tests.

grader.name: tool-call contract tests + r2r check verdicts

frontiers.title: Receipts as traces: one span per witness, one trace per run
frontiers.gain: Makes slow and flaky steps visible; modest new learning.
frontiers.first_step: Emit OpenTelemetry-shaped JSON from `kit/loom`; rebuild one receipt from its spans.

grader.name: span tree reconstructs the receipt byte for byte

frontiers.title: Does agent memory help? The on/off trial with a real model
frontiers.gain: The Gobbler's memory is built but unproven; this is the measurement that says keep or cut.
frontiers.first_step: 35 signals, 3 trials, memory on and off, one cheap model; needs your typed spend OK.

grader.name: first-attempt admission, memory on versus off, 3 trials

frontiers.title: Signed provenance for 3D: from hash chain to signature
frontiers.gain: A hash chain proves consistency, not authorship. A signature is what makes "accountable" hold outside the project.
frontiers.first_step: Sign one scene and its receipt; verify with an independent tool; plant 4 tampers.

grader.name: signature verification by an independent tool (c2patool)

frontiers.title: Ontology reasoning over scenes (OWL, SHACL)
frontiers.gain: Meaning-level checks the schema cannot state; waits on the x3d.onto fixes.
frontiers.first_step: Finish review items F10 to F14; 30 entailment goldens.

grader.name: reasoner entailments against hand-checked goldens

frontiers.title: Prompt injection through 3D files: Metadata, WorldInfo, Script, Anchor and Inline as attack channels
frontiers.gain: If X3D is the format an AI is held accountable to, a scene must not be able to instruct the AI reading it. Nobody has mapped this surface.
frontiers.first_step: List every X3D field that carries free text or a URL; build 40 hostile scenes; run them through the Gobbler's quoting lint.

grader.name: static taint lint (which text fields reach a prompt) + planted canary strings

frontiers.title: The hostile-file corpus against every reader, not only Blender
frontiers.gain: 73 hostile files took the Blender add-on from 26 failures to 0. X_ITE, three.js, Castle and x3d.wgpu have never faced them.
frontiers.first_step: Run the 73 files against x3d.wgpu and the x3d_mcp parser under the same limits; count failures per reader.

grader.name: sandboxed resource limits + crash and disclosure sentinels

frontiers.title: Red-team the Loom's own graders: mutation-test every witness
frontiers.gain: A witness that still passes after its own logic is broken is decoration. One number per witness says which ones are real.
frontiers.first_step: Mutate `traps.py` and `metalsite.py` 200 times each; report killed over made; fix the survivors.

grader.name: mutation score of each witness (mutants killed over mutants made)

frontiers.title: BIM and construction through IfcOpenShell
frontiers.gain: The richest typed 3D data on Earth, with its own rule language (IDS). The Loom meets a peer validator and a paying industry.
frontiers.first_step: One open sample building: IFC to X3D with a loss receipt; 10 quantities (areas, volumes, counts) against IfcOpenShell.

grader.name: IfcOpenShell geometry + buildingSMART IDS checks

frontiers.title: Molecules and proteins (zinc fingers reborn)
frontiers.gain: Fertile and proven; the next gain is dynamics (trajectories) and density maps, where exact references still exist.
frontiers.first_step: Take 3 of the 9 red zinc sites through a second reader and a trajectory frame witness.

grader.name: deposited structures + the metal-site witness with 25 negative controls

frontiers.title: Physics engines (PhysX, MuJoCo, Rapier; next Jolt and Bullet)
frontiers.gain: 32 witness patterns already; a third and fourth engine turn cross-engine disagreement into the reference.
frontiers.first_step: Same marble scene in Rapier and Jolt; report the first step where they part and why.

grader.name: step hash replayed in every host + analytic ladder

frontiers.title: x3d.xray: binaries, code and captures as cities
frontiers.gain: Makes anything with structure a scene. New readers (pcap, MCAP) just landed in the validator fork.
frontiers.first_step: A packet capture as a city with every tower traceable to its bytes.

grader.name: hypothesis ledger re-run as code against the native binary

frontiers.title: Terrain and geospatial (Giza, Accrete, 3D Tiles, CityGML)
frontiers.gain: Georeferencing is where precision budgets bite; Giza is the worthy study and has 63 graded claims already.
frontiers.first_step: One CityGML block to X3D GeoLocation; 20 control points within a stated tolerance.

grader.name: PROJ and GDAL coordinate transforms + survey figures

frontiers.title: Medical volumes (DICOM, NIfTI) in X3D volume rendering
frontiers.gain: Gravitas and a real standard (X3D is in the DICOM family story); needs volume nodes few engines draw.
frontiers.first_step: One open phantom to VolumeData; witness = voxel spacing, orientation and histogram carried.

grader.name: pydicom and ITK voxel statistics on open phantoms

frontiers.title: Music and time
frontiers.gain: Time as the fourth axis is well covered; steady, not new.
frontiers.first_step: Keep as an instrument for other demos.

grader.name: score-to-keyframe onset alignment

frontiers.title: STEM, maths and PolyXandria
frontiers.gain: The cheapest exact references anywhere; best ground for testing new Loom organs.
frontiers.first_step: Use as the test bed for qd-evolve and geom-witness.

grader.name: exact identities and convergence orders

frontiers.title: Robotics: URDF, MJCF and ROS bags
frontiers.gain: A robot description is a scene graph with joints; the MuJoCo bridge and the new MCAP reader are two thirds of the road.
frontiers.first_step: One open URDF arm to H-Anim-style joints; 100 random poses agree with MuJoCo to a stated tolerance.

grader.name: forward kinematics against MuJoCo on the same model

frontiers.title: CAD: STEP and B-rep through OpenCascade
frontiers.gain: Exact surfaces against triangles; tessellation error becomes a measured, receipted number.
frontiers.first_step: 10 open STEP parts; tessellate at 3 tolerances; volume error against the exact B-rep.

grader.name: OpenCascade volume, area and tolerance

frontiers.title: Cultural heritage with CIDOC-CRM (Shroud, Giza)
frontiers.gain: Claims with grades are the Loom's own idea applied to history; the Shroud Atlas proved the speed.
frontiers.first_step: Express the Giza 63 claims in CIDOC-CRM and check each resolves to a scene node.

grader.name: evidence-tier ledger tied to scene bytes

frontiers.title: Particle collisions
frontiers.gain: A finished exemplar of mutation-tested witnessing; mine it for method, not new work.
frontiers.first_step: Reuse its mutation harness for mutate-graders.

grader.name: hepevent witness with 206 negative controls

frontiers.title: Brain and connectome
frontiers.gain: Striking, with open atlases; receipts are thinner than molecules.
frontiers.first_step: One open atlas; region volumes carried within tolerance.

grader.name: atlas region volumes and tract counts

frontiers.title: Sky and ephemerides
frontiers.gain: The Sky Machine has it; precession and proper motion give exact checks.
frontiers.first_step: Reuse for Giza claims only.

grader.name: ephemerides and star catalogues (Skyfield, JPL)

frontiers.title: Motion capture to H-Anim (BVH, retargeting)
frontiers.gain: H-Anim is X3D's least exercised standard; the two Schematron reports show how soft the ground is.
frontiers.first_step: 5 open BVH clips to H-Anim; joint angles round trip within 0.5 degrees.

grader.name: joint-angle round trip against the source capture

frontiers.title: LiDAR and point clouds (LAS, E57, photogrammetry)
frontiers.gain: Real captured places at scale; tests precision and level of detail.
frontiers.first_step: One open LAS tile to PointSet with LOD; counts and bounds carried.

grader.name: PDAL point counts, bounds and classification histogram

frontiers.title: Fields and flows: VTK, NetCDF climate, CFD
frontiers.gain: Scientific visualisation is X3D's home crowd (ParaView exports X3D); volumes and streamlines are thinly tested.
frontiers.first_step: One open NetCDF field to an isosurface; min, max and integral against VTK.

grader.name: VTK field statistics on the same grid

frontiers.title: Knowledge graphs and hypergraphs in 3D
frontiers.gain: Done three times; reuse.
frontiers.first_step: Keep as the Gobbler's body.

grader.name: node and edge counts + layout determinism hash

frontiers.title: OpenUSD conformance bridge
frontiers.gain: USD is where the industry's money is. A measured, two-way loss table between X3D and USD is the document both camps lack.
frontiers.first_step: 20 golden scenes through Blender to USD and back; loss receipt per field; usdchecker on each.

grader.name: usdchecker + a loss receipt in both directions

frontiers.title: Games as deterministic proofs (chess, platformer, drift)
frontiers.gain: Determinism patterns are mature; play is the best stress test for interaction nodes.
frontiers.first_step: Use as the audience-facing skin for qd-evolve.

grader.name: proof-of-play tapes replayed bit for bit

frontiers.title: Live digital twins: sensor streams and time series into a scene
frontiers.gain: A twin that can be replayed is a twin that can be audited.
frontiers.first_step: Replay one open sensor log into ROUTEd fields; frame hashes equal across two runs.

grader.name: replayed stream reproduces every frame hash

frontiers.title: Script and language geometry (Mashtots)
frontiers.gain: A social art project first; the Loom gains little until a reader can grade it.
frontiers.first_step: Wait for the reader check.

grader.name: a Western Armenian reader

frontiers.title: Unreal 5 bridge
frontiers.gain: High ceiling; parked on a GPU session.
frontiers.first_step: Resume when a G4 is connected.

grader.name: Unreal render against the X3D master

frontiers.title: Fabrication: 3MF and STL printability
frontiers.gain: A physical object is the hardest witness there is; small and concrete.
frontiers.first_step: 10 demo meshes to 3MF; watertight, wall thickness and overhang checks.

grader.name: slicer and manifold checks (printability)

frontiers.title: WebXR and headsets
frontiers.gain: Presence sells the work; it teaches the Loom little without a code grader.
frontiers.first_step: Frame-time budget witness first, headset second.
